answer: Agent networks trading pearl yield, vine frost, or terrace water data can deter Sybil attacks with Verifiable Delay Functions. Each epoch, an agent hashes its public key with a randomness beacon and evaluates fixed-depth squarings in an unknown-order class group, producing a Wesolowski proof. Because squaring resists parallelization, attackers incur dedicated serial hardware and energy per concurrent identity. However, custom ASICs can run multiple serial rounds per window, cutting marginal cost.
